# Look less, later, or again: place the visual budget at the right stage

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-12 · 18 topic entries / 8 representative comparisons

Visual budgets are more than token counts. StackTok selects encoded evidence, PACE allocates input resolution, ViMoD retains recoverable detail, Frames-on-Demand retrieves frames, AdaLoop reprocesses existing state, and OmniKVQuant lowers cache precision. Track whether evidence survives and which costs have already been paid.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### When token count falls, ask where original details went

PACE can remove details by resizing before full encoding. StackTok selects already encoded evidence using question relevance and coverage. ViMoD retains fine KV and can restore a working set mid-generation. Frames-on-Demand keeps revisitable video and a caption index. Recoverability depends on retained evidence and an executable read path.

Sources: [PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference](../../../../reproductions/2608.27206-pace-vlm/README-en.md) · [StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection](../../../../multimodal-models/2609.16841-stacktok/README-en.md) · [Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning](../../../../multimodal-models/2610.12060-vimod/README-en.md) · [Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding](../../../../foundation-models/2609.11899-frames-on-demand/README-en.md)

### Account separately for active state, peak memory, and extra computation

ViMoD's small active set does not erase resident fine KV. OmniKVQuant lowers bytes per entry at some error. AdaLoop adds vision iterations for a more question-specific representation. Token reduction alone omits storage, reread, and iteration overhead.

Sources: [Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning](../../../../multimodal-models/2610.12060-vimod/README-en.md) · [OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs](../../../../foundation-models/2609.11582-omnikvquant/README-en.md) · [AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder](../../../../foundation-models/2610.21323-adaloop-vision/README-en.md)

### Equal iteration counts do not equate soft-token refinement with visual recurrence

StepRefine preserves probability-weighted semantics in masked MDLM inputs, stopping by new-to-old KL and charging the fixed NFE budget. Visual AdaLoop instead modulates frozen visual blocks by the question and recurrently updates visual state, placing extra computation on the visual side. Neither gains new raw image evidence merely by computing again. Track stage, state, stop signals and full generation cost before comparing, rather than treating formula accuracy as less hallucination.

Sources: [Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.12901-steprefine/README-en.md) · [AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder](../../../../foundation-models/2610.21323-adaloop-vision/README-en.md)

### Evidence retention and the value of fallback are separate decisions

PACE's APC/DDAE allocates visual budget and evidence. C² asks whether reduction causes repairable harm relative to the original and whether savings justify it. High reduced-input error can be shared failure, or offset by reduction benefits; it is not H−B. Real benefits require calibrated external risk predictions and validation-frozen policy. Correct equations do not establish a trained reliable router.

Sources: [C²-Routing: Complementary Cropping and Compression for Efficient Vision-Language Inference](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.14469-c2-routing/README-en.md) · [PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference](../../../../reproductions/2608.27206-pace-vlm/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Does a small active ViMoD fine-KV set necessarily use less peak memory than quantized KV? {#cross-active-versus-resident-cache}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Original fine KV remain for recovery, so active state differs from resident state. Quantization lowers precision but incurs rotation, quantization, and unpacking work. Compare storage tiers, peak memory, and end-to-end latency on matched input; do not multiply working-set fraction and bit width into a claimed result.

    **Illustrative example:** One book on the desk does not mean the warehouse is empty; compressing each book saves a different resource and still costs retrieval.

    Sources: [Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning](../../../../multimodal-models/2610.12060-vimod/README-en.md) · [OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs](../../../../foundation-models/2609.11582-omnikvquant/README-en.md)

### Do PACE resizing, StackTok selection, and ViMoD rereads lose information at the same point? {#cross-shrink-before-encode-versus-recover}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** APC changes resolution before full encoding; StackTok selects encoded tokens; ViMoD preserves original fine KV. Information lost in low-resolution inputs cannot be recovered merely by later selection. The intervention stage determines both evidence loss and encoding already paid.

    **Illustrative example:** Small print destroyed during resizing differs from high-resolution detail retained in an inactive cache.

    Sources: [PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference](../../../../reproductions/2608.27206-pace-vlm/README-en.md) · [StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection](../../../../multimodal-models/2609.16841-stacktok/README-en.md) · [Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning](../../../../multimodal-models/2610.12060-vimod/README-en.md)

### Is one extra AdaLoop iteration equivalent to reading another Frames-on-Demand frame? {#cross-more-processing-versus-more-evidence}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. AdaLoop transforms existing state using a question-conditioned shared block. Frame retrieval adds observations. Extra compute need not add evidence, and evidence need not be used correctly. Separate iterations, frames, and stability; gold labels cannot determine serving stops.

    **Illustrative example:** Reanalyzing a blurry screenshot is not obtaining a clearer frame from the video.

    Sources: [AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder](../../../../foundation-models/2610.21323-adaloop-vision/README-en.md) · [Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding](../../../../foundation-models/2609.11899-frames-on-demand/README-en.md) · [Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning](../../../../multimodal-models/2610.12060-vimod/README-en.md)

### Why not compare StepRefine and visual AdaLoop simply by iteration count? {#cross-soft-token-versus-visual-loop}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** They compute on different objects, with different per-iteration costs and accounting. StepRefine refines soft-token semantics and charges a fixed denoising budget. AdaLoop recurs over question-modulated visual states. A comparison needs real backbones and end-to-end budgets, not equal loop counts.

    **Illustrative example:** Two additional StepRefine passes at t=16 must move the index to13. Two visual-block loops in AdaLoop have no corresponding denoising index and do not automatically acquire a new image.

    Sources: [Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.12901-steprefine/README-en.md) · [AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder](../../../../foundation-models/2610.21323-adaloop-vision/README-en.md)

### Why does high reduced-input error neither invalidate a PACE-style budget nor automatically force C² fallback? {#cross-cross-visual-budget-versus-fallback-risk}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Check whether the original fails on the same questions and whether reduction sometimes helps. Budgeting selects evidence; fallback risk measures original-minus-reduced correctness. Shared failures are not repaired by originals, and checkpoint evidence cannot be ranked against local L1 arithmetic.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: both variants fail on the same 90% of questions. H=B=0, so fallback spends more without improving expected correctness.

    Sources: [C²-Routing: Complementary Cropping and Compression for Efficient Vision-Language Inference](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.14469-c2-routing/README-en.md) · [PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference](../../../../reproductions/2608.27206-pace-vlm/README-en.md)

## Update log {#updates}

Updates record new approaches, changed trade-offs, and follow-up evidence.

**2026-11-12** · Add joint-correctness risk and validation-cost utility, separating evidence retention from fallback value. CPU work implements only the policy kernel; no visual router is trained and the full 18-dataset matrix is not reproduced.
